text: LSL permits global variables above the state declarations. Initializer restrictions do not prohibit global state.
Use supported LSL control flow. Ternary expressions and switch statements are unavailable. Code checks here do not replace compilation.
LSL evaluates both operands of logical AND and OR. Do not use these operators to guard an unsafe expression by short-circuiting.
Measure peak script memory under representative workloads. Large temporary lists and strings can exhaust headroom even when steady-state usage looks acceptable.
A synchronous notecard lookup can return NAK when the card is uncached. Retain an asynchronous request path and correlate dataserver replies.
SLua is based on Luau. Its ll namespace, table indexing, types and event model need deliberate migration; renaming llFoo to ll.Foo alone is insufficient.
Conventional array-style table sequences begin at index 1. Lua tables also support other keys, so a key of 0 is not inherently invalid.

Register event callbacks through LLEvents:on. Keep callback references for removal and avoid accumulating duplicate handlers. A function named state_entry does not by itself establish an LSL-style state lifecycle.
LLTimers offers independent recurring and one-shot callbacks. Store returned references and cancel unused callbacks with LLTimers:off. Validate timing behavior in the target simulator.
Use SLua constructors for vector, quaternion and UUID values. Conversion helpers can return nil; verify their current signatures before substituting for LSL casts.
Linden Lab announced the SLua open beta on 2 December 2025. Verify current viewer and region support instead of assuming rollout from this snapshot's review date.

Permission requests replace the existing mask for that script; request every permission still needed. Match the current avatar, permission key and granted mask before taking controls. Use deliberate input ownership and preserve an active user when another avatar changes the linkset.

Linked-message delivery can be lost when event queues fill. Critical request/reply work needs one bounded in-flight request, a session/request identifier, retry/deadline policy, idempotent installation and cleanup of retained replies. A compile pass cannot verify this protocol.

Account for per-call forced delays across loops: a one-second API invoked 30 times can occupy an event for roughly 30 seconds in LSL. Slice cold work across events and reconcile watchdog deadlines. SLua API waits, throttles and scheduling require runtime-specific verification.

Bounded integer millisecond timelines avoid long-uptime float accumulation. Capture paired clock samples before parsing and rebase every live deadline together. Double arithmetic alone does not establish sub-millisecond world synchronization.

Empty caveats and unknown delay data are not evidence of safety. Validate finite values before division, preserve zero-rate stops where valid, and measure actual queue/memory behavior separately from compilation and mocked regression tests.
